Psa.8.6.bsb: You made him ruler of the works of Your hands; You have placed everything under his feet:
Psa.8.6.kjv: Thou madest him to have dominion over the works of thy hands; thou hast put all things under his feet:

Psa.9.13.bsb: Be merciful to me, O LORD; see how my enemies afflict me! Lift me up from the gates of death,
Psa.9.13.kjv: Have mercy upon me, O Lord; consider my trouble which I suffer of them that hate me, thou that liftest me up from the gates of death:

Psa.10.1.bsb: Why, O LORD, do You stand far off? Why do You hide in times of trouble?
Psa.10.1.kjv: Why standest thou afar off, O Lord? why hidest thou thyself in times of trouble?

Psa.102.2.bsb: Do not hide Your face from me in my day of distress. Incline Your ear to me; answer me quickly when I call.
Psa.102.2.kjv: Hide not thy face from me in the day when I am in trouble; incline thine ear unto me: in the day when I call answer me speedily.

Psa.51.11.bsb: Cast me not away from Your presence; take not Your Holy Spirit from me.
Psa.51.11.kjv: Cast me not away from thy presence; and take not thy holy spirit from me.

Psa.4.6.bsb: Many ask, “Who can show us the good?” Shine the light of Your face upon us, O LORD.
Psa.4.6.kjv: There be many that say, Who will shew us any good? Lord, lift thou up the light of thy countenance upon us.

Psa.119.76.bsb: May Your loving devotion comfort me, I pray, according to Your promise to Your servant.
Psa.119.76.kjv: Let, I pray thee, thy merciful kindness be for my comfort, according to thy word unto thy servant.

Psa.39.12.bsb: Hear my prayer, O LORD, and give ear to my cry for help; do not be deaf to my weeping. For I am a foreigner dwelling with You, a stranger like all my fathers.
Psa.39.12.kjv: Hear my prayer, O Lord, and give ear unto my cry; hold not thy peace at my tears: for I am a stranger with thee, and a sojourner, as all my fathers were.

Psa.39.13.bsb: Turn Your gaze away from me, that I may again be cheered before I depart and am no more.”
Psa.39.13.kjv: O spare me, that I may recover strength, before I go hence, and be no more.

Psa.25.17.bsb: The troubles of my heart increase; free me from my distress.
Psa.25.17.kjv: The troubles of my heart are enlarged: O bring thou me out of my distresses.

Psa.25.22.bsb: Redeem Israel, O God, from all its distress.
Psa.25.22.kjv: Redeem Israel, O God, out of all his troubles.

Psa.39.10.bsb: Remove Your scourge from me; I am perishing by the force of Your hand.
Psa.39.10.kjv: Remove thy stroke away from me: I am consumed by the blow of thine hand.

Psa.39.8.bsb: Deliver me from all my transgressions; do not make me the reproach of fools.
Psa.39.8.kjv: Deliver me from all my transgressions: make me not the reproach of the foolish.

Psa.51.1.bsb: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of David. When Nathan the prophet came to him after his adultery with Bathsheba. Have mercy on me, O God, according to Your loving devotion; according to Your great compassion, blot out my transgressions.
Psa.51.1.kjv: To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David, when Nathan the prophet came unto him, after he had gone in to Bath–sheba. Have mercy upon me, O God, according to thy lovingkindness: according unto the multitude of thy tender mercies blot out my transgressions.

Psa.79.8.bsb: Do not hold past sins against us; let Your compassion come quickly, for we are brought low.
Psa.79.8.kjv: O remember not against us former iniquities: let thy tender mercies speedily prevent us: for we are brought very low.

Psa.80.7.bsb: Restore us, O God of Hosts, and cause Your face to shine upon us, that we may be saved.
Psa.80.7.kjv: Turn us again, O God of hosts, and cause thy face to shine; and we shall be saved.

Psa.85.4.bsb: Restore us, O God of our salvation, and put away Your displeasure toward us.
Psa.85.4.kjv: Turn us, O God of our salvation, and cause thine anger toward us to cease.

Psa.85.5.bsb: Will You be angry with us forever? Will You draw out Your anger to all generations?
Psa.85.5.kjv: Wilt thou be angry with us for ever? wilt thou draw out thine anger to all generations?

Psa.85.6.bsb: Will You not revive us again, that Your people may rejoice in You?
Psa.85.6.kjv: Wilt thou not revive us again: that thy people may rejoice in thee?

Psa.27.11.bsb: Teach me Your way, O LORD, and lead me on a level path, because of my oppressors.
Psa.27.11.kjv: Teach me thy way, O Lord, and lead me in a plain path, because of mine enemies.

Psa.143.10.bsb: Teach me to do Your will, for You are my God. May Your good Spirit lead me on level ground.
Psa.143.10.kjv: Teach me to do thy will; for thou art my God: thy spirit is good; lead me into the land of uprightness.

Psa.6.2.bsb: Be merciful to me, O LORD, for I am frail; heal me, O LORD, for my bones are in agony.
Psa.6.2.kjv: Have mercy upon me, O Lord; for I am weak: O Lord, heal me; for my bones are vexed.

Psa.51.8.bsb: Let me hear joy and gladness; let the bones You have crushed rejoice.
Psa.51.8.kjv: Make me to hear joy and gladness; that the bones which thou hast broken may rejoice.

Psa.51.12.bsb: Restore to me the joy of Your salvation, and sustain me with a willing spirit.
Psa.51.12.kjv: Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation; and uphold me with thy free spirit.

Psa.69.29.bsb: But I am in pain and distress; let Your salvation protect me, O God.
Psa.69.29.kjv: But I am poor and sorrowful: let thy salvation, O God, set me up on high.

Psa.90.14.bsb: Satisfy us in the morning with Your loving devotion, that we may sing for joy and be glad all our days.
Psa.90.14.kjv: O satisfy us early with thy mercy; that we may rejoice and be glad all our days.

Psa.90.15.bsb: Make us glad for as many days as You have afflicted us, for as many years as we have seen evil.
Psa.90.15.kjv: Make us glad according to the days wherein thou hast afflicted us, and the years wherein we have seen evil.

Psa.17.8.bsb: Keep me as the apple of Your eye; hide me in the shadow of Your wings
Psa.17.8.kjv: Keep me as the apple of the eye, hide me under the shadow of thy wings,

Psa.17.9.bsb: from the wicked who assail me, from my mortal enemies who surround me.
Psa.17.9.kjv: From the wicked that oppress me, from my deadly enemies, who compass me about.

Psa.39.4.bsb: “Show me, O LORD, my end and the measure of my days. Let me know how fleeting my life is.
Psa.39.4.kjv: Lord, make me to know mine end, and the measure of my days, what it is; that I may know how frail I am.

Psa.143.11.bsb: For the sake of Your name, O LORD, revive me. In Your righteousness, bring my soul out of trouble.
Psa.143.11.kjv: Quicken me, O Lord, for thy name’s sake: for thy righteousness’ sake bring my soul out of trouble.

Psa.68.17.bsb: The chariots of God are tens of thousands—thousands of thousands are they; the Lord is in His sanctuary as He was at Sinai.
Psa.68.17.kjv: The chariots of God are twenty thousand, even thousands of angels: the Lord is among them, as in Sinai, in the holy place.

Psa.104.4.bsb: He makes the winds His messengers, flames of fire His servants.
Psa.104.4.kjv: Who maketh his angels spirits; his ministers a flaming fire:

Psa.103.20.bsb: Bless the LORD, all His angels mighty in strength who carry out His word, who hearken to the voice of His command.
Psa.103.20.kjv: Bless the Lord, ye his angels, that excel in strength, that do his commandments, hearkening unto the voice of his word.

Psa.103.21.bsb: Bless the LORD, all His hosts, you servants who do His will.
Psa.103.21.kjv: Bless ye the Lord, all ye his hosts; ye ministers of his, that do his pleasure.

Psa.35.5.bsb: May they be like chaff in the wind, as the angel of the LORD drives them away.
Psa.35.5.kjv: Let them be as chaff before the wind: and let the angel of the Lord chase them.

Psa.35.6.bsb: May their path be dark and slick, as the angel of the LORD pursues.
Psa.35.6.kjv: Let their way be dark and slippery: and let the angel of the Lord persecute them.

Psa.148.2.bsb: Praise Him, all His angels; praise Him, all His heavenly hosts.
Psa.148.2.kjv: Praise ye him, all his angels: praise ye him, all his hosts.

Psa.34.7.bsb: The angel of the LORD encamps around those who fear Him, and he delivers them.
Psa.34.7.kjv: The angel of the Lord encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivereth them.

Psa.91.11.bsb: For He will command His angels concerning you to guard you in all your ways.
Psa.91.11.kjv: For he shall give his angels charge over thee, to keep thee in all thy ways.

Psa.91.12.bsb: They will lift you up in their hands, so that you will not strike your foot against a stone.
Psa.91.12.kjv: They shall bear thee up in their hands, lest thou dash thy foot against a stone.

Psa.133.2.bsb: It is like fine oil on the head, running down on the beard, running down Aaron’s beard over the collar of his robes.
Psa.133.2.kjv: It is like the precious ointment upon the head, that ran down upon the beard, even Aaron’s beard: that went down to the skirts of his garments;

Psa.118.22.bsb: The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone.
Psa.118.22.kjv: The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner.

Psa.68.18.bsb: You have ascended on high; You have led captives away. You have received gifts from men, even from the rebellious, that the LORD God may dwell there.
Psa.68.18.kjv: Thou hast ascended on high, thou hast led captivity captive: thou hast received gifts for men; yea, for the rebellious also, that the Lord God might dwell among them.

Psa.99.7.bsb: He spoke to them from the pillar of cloud; they kept His decrees and the statutes He gave them.
Psa.99.7.kjv: He spake unto them in the cloudy pillar: they kept his testimonies, and the ordinance that he gave them.

Psa.105.39.bsb: He spread a cloud as a covering and a fire to light up the night.
Psa.105.39.kjv: He spread a cloud for a covering; and fire to give light in the night.

Psa.104.30.bsb: When You send Your Spirit, they are created, and You renew the face of the earth.
Psa.104.30.kjv: Thou sendest forth thy spirit, they are created: and thou renewest the face of the earth.

Psa.33.9.bsb: For He spoke, and it came to be; He commanded, and it stood firm.
Psa.33.9.kjv: For he spake, and it was done; he commanded, and it stood fast.

Psa.135.6.bsb: The LORD does all that pleases Him in the heavens and on the earth, in the seas and in all their depths.
Psa.135.6.kjv: Whatsoever the Lord pleased, that did he in heaven, and in earth, in the seas, and all deep places.

Psa.19.1.bsb: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of David. The heavens declare the glory of God; the skies proclaim the work of His hands.
Psa.19.1.kjv: To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David. The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament sheweth his handywork.

Psa.104.24.bsb: How many are Your works, O LORD! In wisdom You have made them all; the earth is full of Your creatures.
Psa.104.24.kjv: O Lord, how manifold are thy works! in wisdom hast thou made them all: the earth is full of thy riches.

Psa.136.5.bsb: By His insight He made the heavens. His loving devotion endures forever.
Psa.136.5.kjv: To him that by wisdom made the heavens: for his mercy endureth for ever.

Psa.33.5.bsb: The LORD loves righteousness and justice; the earth is full of His loving devotion.
Psa.33.5.kjv: He loveth righteousness and judgment: the earth is full of the goodness of the Lord.

Psa.145.10.bsb: All You have made will give You thanks, O LORD, and Your saints will bless You.
Psa.145.10.kjv: All thy works shall praise thee, O Lord; and thy saints shall bless thee.

Psa.148.5.bsb: Let them praise the name of the LORD, for He gave the command and they were created.
Psa.148.5.kjv: Let them praise the name of the Lord: for he commanded, and they were created.

Psa.146.5.bsb: Blessed is he whose help is the God of Jacob, whose hope is in the LORD his God,
Psa.146.5.kjv: Happy is he that hath the God of Jacob for his help, whose hope is in the Lord his God:

Psa.146.6.bsb: the Maker of heaven and earth, the sea, and everything in them. He remains faithful forever.
Psa.146.6.kjv: Which made heaven, and earth, the sea, and all that therein is: which keepeth truth for ever:

Psa.124.8.bsb: Our help is in the name of the LORD, the Maker of heaven and earth.
Psa.124.8.kjv: Our help is in the name of the Lord, who made heaven and earth.

Psa.8.3.bsb: When I behold Your heavens, the work of Your fingers, the moon and the stars, which You have set in place—
Psa.8.3.kjv: When I consider thy heavens, the work of thy fingers, the moon and the stars, which thou hast ordained;

Psa.8.4.bsb: what is man that You are mindful of him, or the son of man that You care for him?
Psa.8.4.kjv: What is man, that thou art mindful of him? and the son of man, that thou visitest him?

Psa.51.10.bsb: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me.
Psa.51.10.kjv: Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me.

Psa.45.2.bsb: You are the most handsome of men; grace has anointed your lips; therefore God has blessed you forever.
Psa.45.2.kjv: Thou art fairer than the children of men: grace is poured into thy lips: therefore God hath blessed thee for ever.

Psa.110.4.bsb: The LORD has sworn and will not change His mind: “You are a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek.”
Psa.110.4.kjv: The Lord hath sworn, and will not repent, Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek.

Psa.72.17.bsb: May his name endure forever; may his name continue as long as the sun shines. In him may all nations be blessed; may they call him blessed.
Psa.72.17.kjv: His name shall endure for ever: his name shall be continued as long as the sun: and men shall be blessed in him: all nations shall call him blessed.

Psa.102.16.bsb: For the LORD will rebuild Zion; He has appeared in His glory.
Psa.102.16.kjv: When the Lord shall build up Zion, he shall appear in his glory.

Psa.45.11.bsb: and the king will desire your beauty; bow to him, for he is your lord.
Psa.45.11.kjv: So shall the king greatly desire thy beauty: for he is thy Lord; and worship thou him.

Psa.96.6.bsb: Splendor and majesty are before Him; strength and beauty fill His sanctuary.
Psa.96.6.kjv: Honour and majesty are before him: strength and beauty are in his sanctuary.

Psa.45.13.bsb: All glorious is the princess in her chamber; her gown is embroidered with gold.
Psa.45.13.kjv: The king’s daughter is all glorious within: her clothing is of wrought gold.

Psa.45.14.bsb: In colorful garments she is led to the king; her virgin companions are brought before you.
Psa.45.14.kjv: She shall be brought unto the king in raiment of needlework: the virgins her companions that follow her shall be brought unto thee.

Psa.48.8.bsb: As we have heard, so we have seen in the city of the LORD of Hosts, in the city of our God: God will establish her forever. Selah
Psa.48.8.kjv: As we have heard, so have we seen in the city of the Lord of hosts, in the city of our God: God will establish it for ever. Selah.

Psa.48.2.bsb: Beautiful in loftiness, the joy of all the earth, like the peaks of Zaphon is Mount Zion, the city of the great King.
Psa.48.2.kjv: Beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is mount Zion, on the sides of the north, the city of the great King.

Psa.50.2.bsb: From Zion, perfect in beauty, God shines forth.
Psa.50.2.kjv: Out of Zion, the perfection of beauty, God hath shined.

Psa.48.12.bsb: March around Zion, encircle her, count her towers,
Psa.48.12.kjv: Walk about Zion, and go round about her: tell the towers thereof.

Psa.48.13.bsb: consider her ramparts, tour her citadels, that you may tell the next generation.
Psa.48.13.kjv: Mark ye well her bulwarks, consider her palaces; that ye may tell it to the generation following.

Psa.51.5.bsb: Surely I was brought forth in iniquity; I was sinful when my mother conceived me.
Psa.51.5.kjv: Behold, I was shapen in iniquity; and in sin did my mother conceive me.

Psa.10.5.bsb: He is secure in his ways at all times; Your lofty judgments are far from him; he sneers at all his foes.
Psa.10.5.kjv: His ways are always grievous; thy judgments are far above out of his sight: as for all his enemies, he puffeth at them.

Psa.14.2.bsb: The LORD looks down from heaven upon the sons of men to see if any understand, if any seek God.
Psa.14.2.kjv: The Lord looked down from heaven upon the children of men, to see if there were any that did understand, and seek God.

Psa.14.3.bsb: All have turned away, they have together become corrupt; there is no one who does good, not even one.
Psa.14.3.kjv: They are all gone aside, they are all together become filthy: there is none that doeth good, no, not one.

Psa.58.3.bsb: The wicked are estranged from the womb; the liars go astray from birth.
Psa.58.3.kjv: The wicked are estranged from the womb: they go astray as soon as they be born, speaking lies.

Psa.3.3.bsb: But You, O LORD, are a shield around me, my glory, and the One who lifts my head.
Psa.3.3.kjv: But thou, O Lord, art a shield for me; my glory, and the lifter up of mine head.

Psa.84.11.bsb: For the LORD God is a sun and a shield; the LORD gives grace and glory; He withholds no good thing from those who walk with integrity.
Psa.84.11.kjv: For the Lord God is a sun and shield: the Lord will give grace and glory: no good thing will he withhold from them that walk uprightly.

Psa.73.24.bsb: You guide me with Your counsel, and later receive me in glory.
Psa.73.24.kjv: Thou shalt guide me with thy counsel, and afterward receive me to glory.

Psa.93.1.bsb: The LORD reigns! He is robed in majesty; the LORD has clothed and armed Himself with strength. The world indeed is firmly established; it cannot be moved.
Psa.93.1.kjv: The Lord reigneth, he is clothed with majesty; the Lord is clothed with strength, wherewith he hath girded himself: the world also is stablished, that it cannot be moved.

Psa.104.1.bsb: Bless the LORD, O my soul! O LORD my God, You are very great; You are clothed with splendor and majesty.
Psa.104.1.kjv: Bless the Lord, O my soul. O Lord my God, thou art very great; thou art clothed with honour and majesty.

Psa.145.5.bsb: the glorious splendor of Your majesty. And I will meditate on Your wondrous works.
Psa.145.5.kjv: I will speak of the glorious honour of thy majesty, and of thy wondrous works.

Psa.145.12.bsb: to make known to men Your mighty acts and the glorious splendor of Your kingdom.
Psa.145.12.kjv: To make known to the sons of men his mighty acts, and the glorious majesty of his kingdom.

Psa.111.3.bsb: Splendid and majestic is His work; His righteousness endures forever.
Psa.111.3.kjv: His work is honourable and glorious: and his righteousness endureth for ever.

Psa.138.5.bsb: They will sing of the ways of the LORD, for the glory of the LORD is great.
Psa.138.5.kjv: Yea, they shall sing in the ways of the Lord: for great is the glory of the Lord.

Psa.104.31.bsb: May the glory of the LORD endure forever; may the LORD rejoice in His works.
Psa.104.31.kjv: The glory of the Lord shall endure for ever: the Lord shall rejoice in his works.

Psa.8.1.bsb: For the choirmaster. According to Gittith. A Psalm of David. O LORD, our Lord, how majestic is Your name in all the earth! You have set Your glory above the heavens.
Psa.8.1.kjv: To the chief Musician upon Gittith, A Psalm of David. O Lord our Lord, how excellent is thy name in all the earth! who hast set thy glory above the heavens.

Psa.113.4.bsb: The LORD is exalted over all the nations, His glory above the heavens.
Psa.113.4.kjv: The Lord is high above all nations, and his glory above the heavens.

Psa.63.2.bsb: So I have seen You in the sanctuary and beheld Your power and glory.
Psa.63.2.kjv: To see thy power and thy glory, so as I have seen thee in the sanctuary.

Psa.90.16.bsb: May Your work be shown to Your servants, and Your splendor to their children.
Psa.90.16.kjv: Let thy work appear unto thy servants, and thy glory unto their children.

Psa.79.9.bsb: Help us, O God of our salvation, for the glory of Your name; deliver us and atone for our sins, for the sake of Your name.
Psa.79.9.kjv: Help us, O God of our salvation, for the glory of thy name: and deliver us, and purge away our sins, for thy name’s sake.

Psa.145.11.bsb: They will tell of the glory of Your kingdom and speak of Your might,
Psa.145.11.kjv: They shall speak of the glory of thy kingdom, and talk of thy power;

Psa.57.5.bsb: Be exalted, O God, above the heavens; may Your glory cover all the earth.
Psa.57.5.kjv: Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens; let thy glory be above all the earth.

Psa.68.21.bsb: Surely God will crush the heads of His enemies, the hairy crowns of those who persist in guilty ways.
Psa.68.21.kjv: But God shall wound the head of his enemies, and the hairy scalp of such an one as goeth on still in his trespasses.

Psa.40.12.bsb: For evils without number surround me; my sins have overtaken me, so that I cannot see. They are more than the hairs of my head, and my heart has failed within me.
Psa.40.12.kjv: For innumerable evils have compassed me about: mine iniquities have taken hold upon me, so that I am not able to look up; they are more than the hairs of mine head: therefore my heart faileth me.

Psa.69.4.bsb: Those who hate me without cause outnumber the hairs of my head; many are those who would destroy me—my enemies for no reason. Though I did not steal, I must repay.
Psa.69.4.kjv: They that hate me without a cause are more than the hairs of mine head: they that would destroy me, being mine enemies wrongfully, are mighty: then I restored that which I took not away.

Psa.71.18.bsb: Even when I am old and gray, do not forsake me, O God, until I proclaim Your power to the next generation, Your might to all who are to come.
Psa.71.18.kjv: Now also when I am old and grayheaded, O God, forsake me not; until I have shewed thy strength unto this generation, and thy power to every one that is to come.

Psa.22.7.bsb: All who see me mock me; they sneer and shake their heads:
Psa.22.7.kjv: All they that see me laugh me to scorn: they shoot out the lip, they shake the head, saying,

Psa.109.25.bsb: I am an object of scorn to my accusers; when they see me, they shake their heads.
Psa.109.25.kjv: I became also a reproach unto them: when they looked upon me they shaked their heads.

Psa.140.7.bsb: O GOD the Lord, the strength of my salvation, You shield my head in the day of battle.
Psa.140.7.kjv: O God the Lord, the strength of my salvation, thou hast covered my head in the day of battle.

Psa.83.2.bsb: See how Your enemies rage, how Your foes have reared their heads.
Psa.83.2.kjv: For, lo, thine enemies make a tumult: and they that hate thee have lifted up the head.

Psa.27.6.bsb: Then my head will be held high above my enemies around me. At His tabernacle I will offer sacrifices with shouts of joy; I will sing and make music to the LORD.
Psa.27.6.kjv: And now shall mine head be lifted up above mine enemies round about me: therefore will I offer in his tabernacle sacrifices of joy; I will sing, yea, I will sing praises unto the Lord.

Psa.23.5.bsb: You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies. You anoint my head with oil; my cup overflows.
Psa.23.5.kjv: Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies: thou anointest my head with oil; my cup runneth over.

Psa.92.10.bsb: But You have exalted my horn like that of a wild ox; with fine oil I have been anointed.
Psa.92.10.kjv: But my horn shalt thou exalt like the horn of an unicorn: I shall be anointed with fresh oil.

Psa.22.16.bsb: For dogs surround me; a band of evil men encircles me; they have pierced my hands and feet.
Psa.22.16.kjv: For dogs have compassed me: the assembly of the wicked have inclosed me: they pierced my hands and my feet.

Psa.89.35.bsb: Once and for all I have sworn by My holiness—I will not lie to David—
Psa.89.35.kjv: Once have I sworn by my holiness that I will not lie unto David.

Psa.89.36.bsb: his offspring shall endure forever, and his throne before Me like the sun,
Psa.89.36.kjv: His seed shall endure for ever, and his throne as the sun before me.

Psa.133.1.bsb: A song of ascents. Of David. Behold, how good and pleasant it is when brothers live together in harmony!
Psa.133.1.kjv: A Song of degrees of David. Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!

Psa.16.2.bsb: I said to the LORD, “You are my Lord; apart from You I have no good thing.”
Psa.16.2.kjv: O my soul, thou hast said unto the Lord, Thou art my Lord: my goodness extendeth not to thee;

Psa.139.14.bsb: I praise You, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made. Marvelous are Your works, and I know this very well.
Psa.139.14.kjv: I will praise thee; for I am fearfully and wonderfully made: marvellous are thy works; and that my soul knoweth right well.

Psa.8.5.bsb: You made him a little lower than the angels; You crowned him with glory and honor.
Psa.8.5.kjv: For thou hast made him a little lower than the angels, and hast crowned him with glory and honour.

Psa.8.7.bsb: all sheep and oxen, and even the beasts of the field,
Psa.8.7.kjv: All sheep and oxen, yea, and the beasts of the field;

Psa.8.8.bsb: the birds of the air and the fish of the sea, all that swim the paths of the seas.
Psa.8.8.kjv: The fowl of the air, and the fish of the sea, and whatsoever passeth through the paths of the seas.

Psa.144.4.bsb: Man is like a breath; his days are like a passing shadow.
Psa.144.4.kjv: Man is like to vanity: his days are as a shadow that passeth away.

Psa.90.5.bsb: You sweep them away in their sleep; they are like the new grass of the morning—
Psa.90.5.kjv: Thou carriest them away as with a flood; they are as a sleep: in the morning they are like grass which groweth up.

Psa.90.10.bsb: The length of our days is seventy years—or eighty if we are strong—yet their pride is but labor and sorrow, for they quickly pass, and we fly away.
Psa.90.10.kjv: The days of our years are threescore years and ten; and if by reason of strength they be fourscore years, yet is their strength labour and sorrow; for it is soon cut off, and we fly away.

Psa.39.6.bsb: Surely every man goes about like a phantom; surely he bustles in vain; he heaps up riches not knowing who will haul them away.
Psa.39.6.kjv: Surely every man walketh in a vain shew: surely they are disquieted in vain: he heapeth up riches, and knoweth not who shall gather them.

Psa.94.10.bsb: He who admonishes the nations, does He not discipline? He who teaches man, does He lack knowledge?
Psa.94.10.kjv: He that chastiseth the heathen, shall not he correct? he that teacheth man knowledge, shall not he know?

Psa.36.6.bsb: Your righteousness is like the highest mountains; Your judgments are like the deepest sea. O LORD, You preserve man and beast.
Psa.36.6.kjv: Thy righteousness is like the great mountains; thy judgments are a great deep: O Lord, thou preservest man and beast.

Psa.145.15.bsb: The eyes of all look to You, and You give them their food in season.
Psa.145.15.kjv: The eyes of all wait upon thee; and thou givest them their meat in due season.

Psa.145.16.bsb: You open Your hand and satisfy the desire of every living thing.
Psa.145.16.kjv: Thou openest thine hand, and satisfiest the desire of every living thing.

Psa.76.10.bsb: Even the wrath of man shall praise You; with the survivors of wrath You will clothe Yourself.
Psa.76.10.kjv: Surely the wrath of man shall praise thee: the remainder of wrath shalt thou restrain.

Psa.39.11.bsb: You discipline and correct a man for his iniquity, consuming like a moth what he holds dear; surely each man is but a vapor. Selah
Psa.39.11.kjv: When thou with rebukes dost correct man for iniquity, thou makest his beauty to consume away like a moth: surely every man is vanity. Selah.

Psa.90.3.bsb: You return man to dust, saying, “Return, O sons of mortals.”
Psa.90.3.kjv: Thou turnest man to destruction; and sayest, Return, ye children of men.

Psa.143.2.bsb: Do not bring Your servant into judgment, for no one alive is righteous before You.
Psa.143.2.kjv: And enter not into judgment with thy servant: for in thy sight shall no man living be justified.

Psa.62.12.bsb: and loving devotion to You, O Lord. For You will repay each man according to his deeds.
Psa.62.12.kjv: Also unto thee, O Lord, belongeth mercy: for thou renderest to every man according to his work.

Psa.118.8.bsb: It is better to take refuge in the LORD than to trust in man.
Psa.118.8.kjv: It is better to trust in the Lord than to put confidence in man.

Psa.60.11.bsb: Give us aid against the enemy, for the help of man is worthless.
Psa.60.11.kjv: Give us help from trouble: for vain is the help of man.

Psa.22.14.bsb: I am poured out like water, and all my bones are disjointed. My heart is like wax; it melts away within me.
Psa.22.14.kjv: I am poured out like water, and all my bones are out of joint: my heart is like wax; it is melted in the midst of my bowels.

Psa.22.15.bsb: My strength is dried up like a potsherd, and my tongue sticks to the roof of my mouth. You lay me in the dust of death.
Psa.22.15.kjv: My strength is dried up like a potsherd; and my tongue cleaveth to my jaws; and thou hast brought me into the dust of death.

Psa.23.4.bsb: Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for You are with me; Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me.
Psa.23.4.kjv: Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff they comfort me.

Psa.5.2.bsb: Attend to the sound of my cry, my King and my God, for to You I pray.
Psa.5.2.kjv: Hearken unto the voice of my cry, my King, and my God: for unto thee will I pray.

Psa.10.17.bsb: You have heard, O LORD, the desire of the humble; You will strengthen their hearts. You will incline Your ear,
Psa.10.17.kjv: Lord, thou hast heard the desire of the humble: thou wilt prepare their heart, thou wilt cause thine ear to hear:

Psa.65.2.bsb: O You who listen to prayer, all people will come to You.
Psa.65.2.kjv: O thou that hearest prayer, unto thee shall all flesh come.

Psa.99.6.bsb: Moses and Aaron were among His priests; Samuel was among those who called on His name. They called to the LORD and He answered.
Psa.99.6.kjv: Moses and Aaron among his priests, and Samuel among them that call upon his name; they called upon the Lord, and he answered them.

Psa.5.3.bsb: In the morning, O LORD, You hear my voice; at daybreak I lay my plea before You and wait in expectation.
Psa.5.3.kjv: My voice shalt thou hear in the morning, O Lord; in the morning will I direct my prayer unto thee, and will look up.

Psa.25.1.bsb: Of David. To You, O LORD, I lift up my soul;
Psa.25.1.kjv: A Psalm of David. Unto thee, O Lord, do I lift up my soul.

Psa.62.8.bsb: Trust in Him at all times, O people; pour out your hearts before Him. God is our refuge. Selah
Psa.62.8.kjv: Trust in him at all times; ye people, pour out your heart before him: God is a refuge for us. Selah.

Psa.116.4.bsb: Then I called on the name of the LORD: “O LORD, deliver my soul!”
Psa.116.4.kjv: Then called I upon the name of the Lord; O Lord, I beseech thee, deliver my soul.

Psa.27.7.bsb: Hear, O LORD, my voice when I call; be merciful and answer me.
Psa.27.7.kjv: Hear, O Lord, when I cry with my voice: have mercy also upon me, and answer me.

Psa.34.6.bsb: This poor man called out, and the LORD heard him; He saved him from all his troubles.
Psa.34.6.kjv: This poor man cried, and the Lord heard him, and saved him out of all his troubles.

Psa.73.28.bsb: But as for me, it is good to draw near to God. I have made the Lord GOD my refuge, that I may proclaim all Your works.
Psa.73.28.kjv: But it is good for me to draw near to God: I have put my trust in the Lord God, that I may declare all thy works.

Psa.27.8.bsb: My heart said, “Seek His face.” Your face, O LORD, I will seek.
Psa.27.8.kjv: When thou saidst, Seek ye my face; my heart said unto thee, Thy face, Lord, will I seek.

Psa.80.18.bsb: Then we will not turn away from You; revive us, and we will call on Your name.
Psa.80.18.kjv: So will not we go back from thee: quicken us, and we will call upon thy name.

Psa.119.58.bsb: I have sought Your face with all my heart; be gracious to me according to Your promise.
Psa.119.58.kjv: I intreated thy favour with my whole heart: be merciful unto me according to thy word.

Psa.119.145.bsb: I call with all my heart; answer me, O LORD! I will obey Your statutes.
Psa.119.145.kjv: ק KOPH. I cried with my whole heart; hear me, O Lord: I will keep thy statutes.

Psa.42.4.bsb: These things come to mind as I pour out my soul: how I walked with the multitude, leading the festive procession to the house of God with shouts of joy and praise.
Psa.42.4.kjv: When I remember these things, I pour out my soul in me: for I had gone with the multitude, I went with them to the house of God, with the voice of joy and praise, with a multitude that kept holyday.

Psa.56.9.bsb: Then my enemies will retreat on the day I cry for help. By this I will know that God is on my side.
Psa.56.9.kjv: When I cry unto thee, then shall mine enemies turn back: this I know; for God is for me.

Psa.86.7.bsb: In the day of my distress I call on You, because You answer me.
Psa.86.7.kjv: In the day of my trouble I will call upon thee: for thou wilt answer me.

Psa.17.1.bsb: A prayer of David. Hear, O LORD, my righteous plea; listen to my cry. Give ear to my prayer—it comes from lips free of deceit.
Psa.17.1.kjv: A Prayer of David. Hear the right, O Lord, attend unto my cry, give ear unto my prayer, that goeth not out of feigned lips.

Psa.145.18.bsb: The LORD is near to all who call on Him, to all who call out to Him in truth.
Psa.145.18.kjv: The Lord is nigh unto all them that call upon him, to all that call upon him in truth.

Psa.55.1.bsb: For the choirmaster. With stringed instruments. A Maskil of David. Listen to my prayer, O God, and do not ignore my plea.
Psa.55.1.kjv: To the chief Musician on Neginoth, Maschil, A Psalm of David. Give ear to my prayer, O God; and hide not thyself from my supplication.

Psa.55.2.bsb: Attend to me and answer me. I am restless in my complaint, and distraught
Psa.55.2.kjv: Attend unto me, and hear me: I mourn in my complaint, and make a noise;

Psa.61.1.bsb: For the choirmaster. With stringed instruments. Of David. Hear my cry, O God; attend to my prayer.
Psa.61.1.kjv: To the chief Musician upon Neginah, A Psalm of David. Hear my cry, O God; attend unto my prayer.

Psa.108.6.bsb: Respond and save us with Your right hand, that Your beloved may be delivered.
Psa.108.6.kjv: That thy beloved may be delivered: save with thy right hand, and answer me.

Psa.143.1.bsb: A Psalm of David. O LORD, hear my prayer. In Your faithfulness, give ear to my plea; in Your righteousness, answer me.
Psa.143.1.kjv: A Psalm of David. Hear my prayer, O Lord, give ear to my supplications: in thy faithfulness answer me, and in thy righteousness.

Psa.66.17.bsb: I cried out to Him with my mouth and praised Him with my tongue.
Psa.66.17.kjv: I cried unto him with my mouth, and he was extolled with my tongue.

Psa.119.49.bsb: Remember Your word to Your servant, upon which You have given me hope.
Psa.119.49.kjv: ז ZAIN. Remember the word unto thy servant, upon which thou hast caused me to hope.

Psa.119.147.bsb: I rise before dawn and cry for help; in Your word I have put my hope.
Psa.119.147.kjv: I prevented the dawning of the morning, and cried: I hoped in thy word.

Psa.95.6.bsb: O come, let us worship and bow down; let us kneel before the LORD our Maker.
Psa.95.6.kjv: O come, let us worship and bow down: let us kneel before the Lord our maker.

Psa.28.2.bsb: Hear my cry for mercy when I call to You for help, when I lift up my hands toward Your holy sanctuary.
Psa.28.2.kjv: Hear the voice of my supplications, when I cry unto thee, when I lift up my hands toward thy holy oracle.

Psa.4.1.bsb: For the choirmaster. With stringed instruments. A Psalm of David. Answer me when I call, O God of my righteousness! You have relieved my distress; show me grace and hear my prayer.
Psa.4.1.kjv: To the chief Musician on Neginoth, A Psalm of David. Hear me when I call, O God of my righteousness: thou hast enlarged me when I was in distress; have mercy upon me, and hear my prayer.

Psa.112.2.bsb: His descendants will be mighty in the land; the generation of the upright will be blessed.
Psa.112.2.kjv: His seed shall be mighty upon earth: the generation of the upright shall be blessed.

Psa.118.5.bsb: In my distress I called to the LORD, and He answered and set me free.
Psa.118.5.kjv: I called upon the Lord in distress: the Lord answered me, and set me in a large place.

Psa.138.3.bsb: On the day I called, You answered me; You emboldened me and strengthened my soul.
Psa.138.3.kjv: In the day when I cried thou answeredst me, and strengthenedst me with strength in my soul.

Psa.50.15.bsb: Call upon Me in the day of trouble; I will deliver you, and you will honor Me.”
Psa.50.15.kjv: And call upon me in the day of trouble: I will deliver thee, and thou shalt glorify me.

Psa.91.15.bsb: When he calls out to Me, I will answer him; I will be with him in trouble. I will deliver him and honor him.
Psa.91.15.kjv: He shall call upon me, and I will answer him: I will be with him in trouble; I will deliver him, and honour him.

Psa.34.4.bsb: I sought the LORD, and He answered me; He delivered me from all my fears.
Psa.34.4.kjv: I sought the Lord, and he heard me, and delivered me from all my fears.

Psa.40.1.bsb: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of David. I waited patiently for the LORD; He inclined to me and heard my cry.
Psa.40.1.kjv: To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David. I waited patiently for the Lord; and he inclined unto me, and heard my cry.

Psa.145.19.bsb: He fulfills the desires of those who fear Him; He hears their cry and saves them.
Psa.145.19.kjv: He will fulfil the desire of them that fear him: he also will hear their cry, and will save them.

Psa.91.14.bsb: “Because he loves Me, I will deliver him; because he knows My name, I will protect him.
Psa.91.14.kjv: Because he hath set his love upon me, therefore will I deliver him: I will set him on high, because he hath known my name.

Psa.18.6.bsb: In my distress I called upon the LORD; I cried to my God for help. From His temple He heard my voice, and my cry for His help reached His ears.
Psa.18.6.kjv: In my distress I called upon the Lord, and cried unto my God: he heard my voice out of his temple, and my cry came before him, even into his ears.

Psa.106.44.bsb: Nevertheless He heard their cry; He took note of their distress.
Psa.106.44.kjv: Nevertheless he regarded their affliction, when he heard their cry:

Psa.9.12.bsb: For the Avenger of bloodshed remembers; He does not ignore the cry of the afflicted.
Psa.9.12.kjv: When he maketh inquisition for blood, he remembereth them: he forgetteth not the cry of the humble.

Psa.34.15.bsb: The eyes of the LORD are on the righteous, and His ears are inclined to their cry.
Psa.34.15.kjv: The eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous, and his ears are open unto their cry.

Psa.116.1.bsb: I love the LORD, for He has heard my voice—my appeal for mercy.
Psa.116.1.kjv: I love the Lord, because he hath heard my voice and my supplications.

Psa.66.20.bsb: Blessed be God, who has not rejected my prayer or withheld from me His loving devotion!
Psa.66.20.kjv: Blessed be God, which hath not turned away my prayer, nor his mercy from me.

Psa.116.17.bsb: I will offer to You a sacrifice of thanksgiving and call on the name of the LORD.
Psa.116.17.kjv: I will offer to thee the sacrifice of thanksgiving, and will call upon the name of the Lord.

Psa.118.21.bsb: I will give You thanks, for You have answered me, and You have become my salvation.
Psa.118.21.kjv: I will praise thee: for thou hast heard me, and art become my salvation.

Psa.116.2.bsb: Because He has inclined His ear to me, I will call on Him as long as I live.
Psa.116.2.kjv: Because he hath inclined his ear unto me, therefore will I call upon him as long as I live.

Psa.66.18.bsb: If I had cherished iniquity in my heart, the Lord would not have listened.
Psa.66.18.kjv: If I regard iniquity in my heart, the Lord will not hear me:

Psa.18.40.bsb: You have made my enemies retreat before me; I destroyed those who hated me.
Psa.18.40.kjv: Thou hast also given me the necks of mine enemies; that I might destroy them that hate me.

Psa.18.41.bsb: They cried for help, but there was no one to save them—to the LORD, but He did not answer.
Psa.18.41.kjv: They cried, but there was none to save them: even unto the Lord, but he answered them not.

Psa.122.6.bsb: Pray for the peace of Jerusalem: “May those who love you prosper.
Psa.122.6.kjv: Pray for the peace of Jerusalem: they shall prosper that love thee.

Psa.55.17.bsb: Morning, noon, and night, I cry out in distress, and He hears my voice.
Psa.55.17.kjv: Evening, and morning, and at noon, will I pray, and cry aloud: and he shall hear my voice.

Psa.88.1.bsb: A song. A Psalm of the sons of Korah. For the choirmaster. According to Mahalath Leannoth. A Maskil of Heman the Ezrahite. O LORD, the God of my salvation, day and night I cry out before You.
Psa.88.1.kjv: A Song or Psalm for the sons of Korah, to the chief Musician upon Mahalath Leannoth, Maschil of Heman the Ezrahite. O Lord God of my salvation, I have cried day and night before thee:

Psa.122.1.bsb: A song of ascents. Of David. I was glad when they said to me, “Let us go to the house of the LORD.”
Psa.122.1.kjv: A Song of degrees of David. I was glad when they said unto me, Let us go into the house of the Lord.

Psa.2.7.bsb: I will proclaim the decree spoken to Me by the LORD: “You are My Son; today I have become Your Father.
Psa.2.7.kjv: I will declare the decree: the Lord hath said unto me, Thou art my Son; this day have I begotten thee.

Psa.132.11.bsb: The LORD swore an oath to David, a promise He will not revoke: “One of your descendants I will place on your throne.
Psa.132.11.kjv: The Lord hath sworn in truth unto David; he will not turn from it; Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne.

Psa.72.10.bsb: May the kings of Tarshish and distant shores bring tribute; may the kings of Sheba and Seba offer gifts.
Psa.72.10.kjv: The kings of Tarshish and of the isles shall bring presents: the kings of Sheba and Seba shall offer gifts.

Psa.45.7.bsb: You have loved righteousness and hated wickedness; therefore God, your God, has anointed you above your companions with the oil of joy.
Psa.45.7.kjv: Thou lovest righteousness, and hatest wickedness: therefore God, thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.

Psa.69.9.bsb: because zeal for Your house has consumed me, and the insults of those who insult You have fallen on me.
Psa.69.9.kjv: For the zeal of thine house hath eaten me up; and the reproaches of them that reproached thee are fallen upon me.

Psa.78.2.bsb: I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter things hidden from the beginning,
Psa.78.2.kjv: I will open my mouth in a parable: I will utter dark sayings of old:

Psa.22.6.bsb: But I am a worm and not a man, scorned by men and despised by the people.
Psa.22.6.kjv: But I am a worm, and no man; a reproach of men, and despised of the people.

Psa.69.7.bsb: For I have endured scorn for Your sake, and shame has covered my face.
Psa.69.7.kjv: Because for thy sake I have borne reproach; shame hath covered my face.

Psa.69.20.bsb: Insults have broken my heart, and I am in despair. I looked for sympathy, but there was none, for comforters, but I found no one.
Psa.69.20.kjv: Reproach hath broken my heart; and I am full of heaviness: and I looked for some to take pity, but there was none; and for comforters, but I found none.

Psa.69.8.bsb: I have become a stranger to my brothers and a foreigner to my mother’s sons,
Psa.69.8.kjv: I am become a stranger unto my brethren, and an alien unto my mother’s children.

Psa.2.1.bsb: Why do the nations rage and the peoples plot in vain?
Psa.2.1.kjv: Why do the heathen rage, and the people imagine a vain thing?

Psa.2.2.bsb: The kings of the earth take their stand and the rulers gather together, against the LORD and against His Anointed One:
Psa.2.2.kjv: The kings of the earth set themselves, and the rulers take counsel together, against the Lord, and against his anointed, saying,

Psa.41.9.bsb: Even my close friend whom I trusted, the one who shared my bread, has lifted up his heel against me.
Psa.41.9.kjv: Yea, mine own familiar friend, in whom I trusted, which did eat of my bread, hath lifted up his heel against me.

Psa.55.12.bsb: For it is not an enemy who insults me; that I could endure. It is not a foe who rises against me; from him I could hide.
Psa.55.12.kjv: For it was not an enemy that reproached me; then I could have borne it: neither was it he that hated me that did magnify himself against me; then I would have hid myself from him:

Psa.55.13.bsb: But it is you, a man like myself, my companion and close friend.
Psa.55.13.kjv: But it was thou, a man mine equal, my guide, and mine acquaintance.

Psa.55.14.bsb: We shared sweet fellowship together; we walked with the crowd into the house of God.
Psa.55.14.kjv: We took sweet counsel together, and walked unto the house of God in company.

Psa.22.1.bsb: For the choirmaster. To the tune of “The Doe of the Dawn.” A Psalm of David. My God, my God, why have You forsaken me? Why are You so far from saving me, so far from my words of groaning?
Psa.22.1.kjv: To the chief Musician upon Aijeleth Shahar, A Psalm of David. My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? why art thou so far from helping me, and from the words of my roaring?

Psa.22.8.bsb: “He trusts in the LORD, let the LORD deliver him; let the LORD rescue him, since He delights in him.”
Psa.22.8.kjv: He trusted on the Lord that he would deliver him: let him deliver him, seeing he delighted in him.

Psa.69.21.bsb: They poisoned my food with gall and gave me vinegar to quench my thirst.
Psa.69.21.kjv: They gave me also gall for my meat; and in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.

Psa.22.18.bsb: They divide my garments among them and cast lots for my clothing.
Psa.22.18.kjv: They part my garments among them, and cast lots upon my vesture.

Psa.34.20.bsb: He protects all his bones; not one of them will be broken.
Psa.34.20.kjv: He keepeth all his bones: not one of them is broken.

Psa.16.10.bsb: For You will not abandon my soul to Sheol, nor will You let Your Holy One see decay.
Psa.16.10.kjv: For thou wilt not leave my soul in hell; neither wilt thou suffer thine Holy One to see corruption.

Psa.110.1.bsb: A Psalm of David. The LORD said to my Lord: “Sit at My right hand until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet.”
Psa.110.1.kjv: A Psalm of David. The Lord said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool.

Psa.2.6.bsb: “I have installed My King on Zion, upon My holy mountain.”
Psa.2.6.kjv: Yet have I set my king upon my holy hill of Zion.

Psa.45.6.bsb: Your throne, O God, endures forever and ever, and justice is the scepter of Your kingdom.
Psa.45.6.kjv: Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: the sceptre of thy kingdom is a right sceptre.

Psa.72.8.bsb: May he rule from sea to sea, and from the Euphrates to the ends of the earth.
Psa.72.8.kjv: He shall have dominion also from sea to sea, and from the river unto the ends of the earth.

Psa.16.8.bsb: I have set the LORD always before me. Because He is at my right hand, I will not be shaken.
Psa.16.8.kjv: I have set the Lord always before me: because he is at my right hand, I shall not be moved.

Psa.16.9.bsb: Therefore my heart is glad and my tongue rejoices; my body also will dwell securely.
Psa.16.9.kjv: Therefore my heart is glad, and my glory rejoiceth: my flesh also shall rest in hope.

Psa.16.11.bsb: You have made known to me the path of life; You will fill me with joy in Your presence, with eternal pleasures at Your right hand.
Psa.16.11.kjv: Thou wilt shew me the path of life: in thy presence is fulness of joy; at thy right hand there are pleasures for evermore.

Psa.74.9.bsb: There are no signs for us to see. There is no longer any prophet. And none of us knows how long this will last.
Psa.74.9.kjv: We see not our signs: there is no more any prophet: neither is there among us any that knoweth how long.

Psa.26.6.bsb: I wash my hands in innocence that I may go about Your altar, O LORD,
Psa.26.6.kjv: I will wash mine hands in innocency: so will I compass thine altar, O Lord:

Psa.76.11.bsb: Make and fulfill your vows to the LORD your God; let all the neighboring lands bring tribute to Him who is to be feared.
Psa.76.11.kjv: Vow, and pay unto the Lord your God: let all that be round about him bring presents unto him that ought to be feared.

Psa.132.2.bsb: how he swore an oath to the LORD, and vowed to the Mighty One of Jacob:
Psa.132.2.kjv: How he sware unto the Lord, and vowed unto the mighty God of Jacob;

Psa.132.3.bsb: “I will not enter my house or get into my bed,
Psa.132.3.kjv: Surely I will not come into the tabernacle of my house, nor go up into my bed;

Psa.132.4.bsb: I will not give sleep to my eyes or slumber to my eyelids,
Psa.132.4.kjv: I will not give sleep to mine eyes, or slumber to mine eyelids,

Psa.132.5.bsb: until I find a place for the LORD, a dwelling for the Mighty One of Jacob.”
Psa.132.5.kjv: Until I find out a place for the Lord, an habitation for the mighty God of Jacob.

Psa.78.63.bsb: Fire consumed His young men, and their maidens were left without wedding songs.
Psa.78.63.kjv: The fire consumed their young men; and their maidens were not given to marriage.

Psa.33.6.bsb: By the word of the LORD the heavens were made, and all the stars by the breath of His mouth.
Psa.33.6.kjv: By the word of the Lord were the heavens made; and all the host of them by the breath of his mouth.

Psa.78.49.bsb: He unleashed His fury against them, wrath, indignation, and calamity—a band of destroying angels.
Psa.78.49.kjv: He cast upon them the fierceness of his anger, wrath, and indignation, and trouble, by sending evil angels among them.

Psa.37.8.bsb: Refrain from anger and abandon wrath; do not fret—it can only bring harm.
Psa.37.8.kjv: Cease from anger, and forsake wrath: fret not thyself in any wise to do evil.

Psa.55.3.bsb: at the voice of the enemy, at the pressure of the wicked. For they bring down disaster upon me and resent me in their anger.
Psa.55.3.kjv: Because of the voice of the enemy, because of the oppression of the wicked: for they cast iniquity upon me, and in wrath they hate me.

Psa.7.11.bsb: God is a righteous judge and a God who feels indignation each day.
Psa.7.11.kjv: God judgeth the righteous, and God is angry with the wicked every day.

Psa.69.24.bsb: Pour out Your wrath upon them, and let Your burning anger overtake them.
Psa.69.24.kjv: Pour out thine indignation upon them, and let thy wrathful anger take hold of them.

Psa.74.1.bsb: A Maskil of Asaph. Why have You rejected us forever, O God? Why does Your anger smolder against the sheep of Your pasture?
Psa.74.1.kjv: Maschil of Asaph. O God, why hast thou cast us off for ever? why doth thine anger smoke against the sheep of thy pasture?

Psa.76.7.bsb: You alone are to be feared. When You are angry, who can stand before You?
Psa.76.7.kjv: Thou, even thou, art to be feared: and who may stand in thy sight when once thou art angry?

Psa.78.21.bsb: Therefore the LORD heard and was filled with wrath; so a fire was kindled against Jacob, and His anger flared against Israel,
Psa.78.21.kjv: Therefore the Lord heard this, and was wroth: so a fire was kindled against Jacob, and anger also came up against Israel;

Psa.78.38.bsb: And yet He was compassionate; He forgave their iniquity and did not destroy them. He often restrained His anger and did not unleash His full wrath.
Psa.78.38.kjv: But he, being full of compassion, forgave their iniquity, and destroyed them not: yea, many a time turned he his anger away, and did not stir up all his wrath.

Psa.78.50.bsb: He cleared a path for His anger; He did not spare them from death but delivered their lives to the plague.
Psa.78.50.kjv: He made a way to his anger; he spared not their soul from death, but gave their life over to the pestilence;

Psa.85.3.bsb: You withheld all Your fury; You turned from Your burning anger.
Psa.85.3.kjv: Thou hast taken away all thy wrath: thou hast turned thyself from the fierceness of thine anger.

Psa.90.11.bsb: Who knows the power of Your anger? Your wrath matches the fear You are due.
Psa.90.11.kjv: Who knoweth the power of thine anger? even according to thy fear, so is thy wrath.

Psa.103.8.bsb: The LORD is compassionate and gracious, slow to anger, abounding in loving devotion.
Psa.103.8.kjv: The Lord is merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and plenteous in mercy.

Psa.106.23.bsb: So He said He would destroy them—had not Moses His chosen one stood before Him in the breach to divert His wrath from destroying them.
Psa.106.23.kjv: Therefore he said that he would destroy them, had not Moses his chosen stood before him in the breach, to turn away his wrath, lest he should destroy them.

Psa.106.29.bsb: So they provoked the LORD to anger with their deeds, and a plague broke out among them.
Psa.106.29.kjv: Thus they provoked him to anger with their inventions: and the plague brake in upon them.

Psa.106.32.bsb: At the waters of Meribah they angered the LORD, and trouble came to Moses because of them.
Psa.106.32.kjv: They angered him also at the waters of strife, so that it went ill with Moses for their sakes:

Psa.110.5.bsb: The Lord is at Your right hand; He will crush kings in the day of His wrath.
Psa.110.5.kjv: The Lord at thy right hand shall strike through kings in the day of his wrath.

Psa.31.2.bsb: Incline Your ear to me; come quickly to my rescue. Be my rock of refuge, the stronghold of my deliverance.
Psa.31.2.kjv: Bow down thine ear to me; deliver me speedily: be thou my strong rock, for an house of defence to save me.

Psa.35.1.bsb: Of David. Contend with my opponents, O LORD; fight against those who fight against me.
Psa.35.1.kjv: A Psalm of David. Plead my cause, O Lord, with them that strive with me: fight against them that fight against me.

Psa.35.2.bsb: Take up Your shield and buckler; arise and come to my aid.
Psa.35.2.kjv: Take hold of shield and buckler, and stand up for mine help.

Psa.35.3.bsb: Draw the spear and javelin against my pursuers; say to my soul: “I am your salvation.”
Psa.35.3.kjv: Draw out also the spear, and stop the way against them that persecute me: say unto my soul, I am thy salvation.

Psa.36.7.bsb: How precious is Your loving devotion, O God, that the children of men take refuge in the shadow of Your wings!
Psa.36.7.kjv: How excellent is thy lovingkindness, O God! therefore the children of men put their trust under the shadow of thy wings.

Psa.57.1.bsb: For the choirmaster. To the tune of “Do Not Destroy.” A Miktam of David, when he fled from Saul into the cave. Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy, for in You my soul takes refuge. In the shadow of Your wings I will take shelter until the danger has passed.
Psa.57.1.kjv: To the chief Musician, Al–taschith, Michtam of David, when he fled from Saul in the cave. Be merciful unto me, O God, be merciful unto me: for my soul trusteth in thee: yea, in the shadow of thy wings will I make my refuge, until these calamities be overpast.

Psa.94.9.bsb: He who affixed the ear, can He not hear? He who formed the eye, can He not see?
Psa.94.9.kjv: He that planted the ear, shall he not hear? he that formed the eye, shall he not see?

Psa.121.4.bsb: Behold, the Protector of Israel will neither slumber nor sleep.
Psa.121.4.kjv: Behold, he that keepeth Israel shall neither slumber nor sleep.

Psa.147.5.bsb: Great is our Lord, and mighty in power; His understanding has no limit.
Psa.147.5.kjv: Great is our Lord, and of great power: his understanding is infinite.

Psa.2.4.bsb: The One enthroned in heaven laughs; the Lord taunts them.
Psa.2.4.kjv: He that sitteth in the heavens shall laugh: the Lord shall have them in derision.

Psa.37.13.bsb: but the Lord laughs, seeing that their day is coming.
Psa.37.13.kjv: The Lord shall laugh at him: for he seeth that his day is coming.

Psa.59.8.bsb: But You, O LORD, laugh at them; You scoff at all the nations.
Psa.59.8.kjv: But thou, O Lord, shalt laugh at them; thou shalt have all the heathen in derision.

Psa.44.23.bsb: Wake up, O Lord! Why are You sleeping? Arise! Do not reject us forever.
Psa.44.23.kjv: Awake, why sleepest thou, O Lord? arise, cast us not off for ever.

Psa.78.61.bsb: He delivered His strength to captivity, and His splendor to the hand of the adversary.
Psa.78.61.kjv: And delivered his strength into captivity, and his glory into the enemy’s hand.

Psa.95.10.bsb: For forty years I was angry with that generation, and I said, “They are a people whose hearts go astray, and they have not known My ways.”
Psa.95.10.kjv: Forty years long was I grieved with this generation, and said, It is a people that do err in their heart, and they have not known my ways:

Psa.44.20.bsb: If we had forgotten the name of our God or spread out our hands to a foreign god,
Psa.44.20.kjv: If we have forgotten the name of our God, or stretched out our hands to a strange god;

Psa.44.21.bsb: would not God have discovered, since He knows the secrets of the heart?
Psa.44.21.kjv: Shall not God search this out? for he knoweth the secrets of the heart.

Psa.73.27.bsb: Those far from You will surely perish; You destroy all who are unfaithful to You.
Psa.73.27.kjv: For, lo, they that are far from thee shall perish: thou hast destroyed all them that go a whoring from thee.

Psa.85.8.bsb: I will listen to what God the LORD will say; for He will surely speak peace to His people and His saints; He will not let them return to folly.
Psa.85.8.kjv: I will hear what God the Lord will speak: for he will speak peace unto his people, and to his saints: but let them not turn again to folly.

Psa.125.5.bsb: But those who turn to crooked ways the LORD will banish with the evildoers. Peace be upon Israel.
Psa.125.5.kjv: As for such as turn aside unto their crooked ways, the Lord shall lead them forth with the workers of iniquity: but peace shall be upon Israel.

Psa.17.5.bsb: My steps have held to Your paths; my feet have not slipped.
Psa.17.5.kjv: Hold up my goings in thy paths, that my footsteps slip not.

Psa.56.13.bsb: For You have delivered my soul from death, and my feet from stumbling, that I may walk before God in the light of life.
Psa.56.13.kjv: For thou hast delivered my soul from death: wilt not thou deliver my feet from falling, that I may walk before God in the light of the living?

Psa.81.13.bsb: If only My people would listen to Me, if Israel would follow My ways,
Psa.81.13.kjv: Oh that my people had hearkened unto me, and Israel had walked in my ways!

Psa.81.14.bsb: how soon I would subdue their enemies and turn My hand against their foes!
Psa.81.14.kjv: I should soon have subdued their enemies, and turned my hand against their adversaries.

Psa.80.3.bsb: Restore us, O God, and cause Your face to shine upon us, that we may be saved.
Psa.80.3.kjv: Turn us again, O God, and cause thy face to shine; and we shall be saved.

Psa.80.4.bsb: O LORD God of Hosts, how long will Your anger smolder against the prayers of Your people?
Psa.80.4.kjv: O Lord God of hosts, how long wilt thou be angry against the prayer of thy people?

Psa.80.5.bsb: You fed them with the bread of tears and made them drink the full measure of their tears.
Psa.80.5.kjv: Thou feedest them with the bread of tears; and givest them tears to drink in great measure.

Psa.80.6.bsb: You make us contend with our neighbors; our enemies mock us.
Psa.80.6.kjv: Thou makest us a strife unto our neighbours: and our enemies laugh among themselves.

Psa.80.14.bsb: Return, O God of Hosts, we pray! Look down from heaven and see! Attend to this vine—
Psa.80.14.kjv: Return, we beseech thee, O God of hosts: look down from heaven, and behold, and visit this vine;

Psa.80.15.bsb: the root Your right hand has planted, the son You have raised up for Yourself.
Psa.80.15.kjv: And the vineyard which thy right hand hath planted, and the branch that thou madest strong for thyself.

Psa.80.16.bsb: Your vine has been cut down and burned; they perish at the rebuke of Your countenance.
Psa.80.16.kjv: It is burned with fire, it is cut down: they perish at the rebuke of thy countenance.

Psa.80.17.bsb: Let Your hand be upon the man at Your right hand, on the son of man You have raised up for Yourself.
Psa.80.17.kjv: Let thy hand be upon the man of thy right hand, upon the son of man whom thou madest strong for thyself.

Psa.80.19.bsb: Restore us, O LORD God of Hosts; cause Your face to shine upon us, that we may be saved.
Psa.80.19.kjv: Turn us again, O Lord God of hosts, cause thy face to shine; and we shall be saved.

Psa.78.10.bsb: They failed to keep God’s covenant and refused to live by His law.
Psa.78.10.kjv: They kept not the covenant of God, and refused to walk in his law;

Psa.78.11.bsb: They forgot what He had done, the wonders He had shown them.
Psa.78.11.kjv: And forgat his works, and his wonders that he had shewed them.

Psa.78.40.bsb: How often they disobeyed Him in the wilderness and grieved Him in the desert!
Psa.78.40.kjv: How oft did they provoke him in the wilderness, and grieve him in the desert!

Psa.78.41.bsb: Again and again they tested God and provoked the Holy One of Israel.
Psa.78.41.kjv: Yea, they turned back and tempted God, and limited the Holy One of Israel.

Psa.78.42.bsb: They did not remember His power—the day He redeemed them from the adversary,
Psa.78.42.kjv: They remembered not his hand, nor the day when he delivered them from the enemy.

Psa.78.43.bsb: when He performed His signs in Egypt and His wonders in the fields of Zoan.
Psa.78.43.kjv: How he had wrought his signs in Egypt, and his wonders in the field of Zoan:

Psa.78.56.bsb: But they tested and disobeyed God Most High, for they did not keep His decrees.
Psa.78.56.kjv: Yet they tempted and provoked the most high God, and kept not his testimonies:

Psa.78.57.bsb: They turned back and were faithless like their fathers, twisted like a faulty bow.
Psa.78.57.kjv: But turned back, and dealt unfaithfully like their fathers: they were turned aside like a deceitful bow.

Psa.78.58.bsb: They enraged Him with their high places and provoked His jealousy with their idols.
Psa.78.58.kjv: For they provoked him to anger with their high places, and moved him to jealousy with their graven images.

Psa.78.59.bsb: On hearing it, God was furious and rejected Israel completely.
Psa.78.59.kjv: When God heard this, he was wroth, and greatly abhorred Israel:

Psa.78.60.bsb: He abandoned the tabernacle of Shiloh, the tent He had pitched among men.
Psa.78.60.kjv: So that he forsook the tabernacle of Shiloh, the tent which he placed among men;

Psa.78.62.bsb: He surrendered His people to the sword because He was enraged by His heritage.
Psa.78.62.kjv: He gave his people over also unto the sword; and was wroth with his inheritance.

Psa.78.64.bsb: His priests fell by the sword, but their widows could not lament.
Psa.78.64.kjv: Their priests fell by the sword; and their widows made no lamentation.

Psa.106.13.bsb: Yet they soon forgot His works and failed to wait for His counsel.
Psa.106.13.kjv: They soon forgat his works; they waited not for his counsel:

Psa.106.14.bsb: They craved intensely in the wilderness and tested God in the desert.
Psa.106.14.kjv: But lusted exceedingly in the wilderness, and tempted God in the desert.

Psa.41.1.bsb: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of David. Blessed is the one who cares for the poor; the LORD will deliver him in the day of trouble.
Psa.41.1.kjv: To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David. Blessed is he that considereth the poor: the Lord will deliver him in time of trouble.

Psa.112.9.bsb: He has scattered abroad his gifts to the poor; his righteousness endures forever; his horn will be lifted high in honor.
Psa.112.9.kjv: He hath dispersed, he hath given to the poor; his righteousness endureth for ever; his horn shall be exalted with honour.

Psa.5.1.bsb: For the choirmaster, to be accompanied by flutes. A Psalm of David. Give ear to my words, O LORD; consider my groaning.
Psa.5.1.kjv: To the chief Musician upon Nehiloth, A Psalm of David. Give ear to my words, O Lord, consider my meditation.

Psa.10.11.bsb: He says to himself, “God has forgotten; He hides His face and never sees.”
Psa.10.11.kjv: He hath said in his heart, God hath forgotten: he hideth his face; he will never see it.

Psa.10.13.bsb: Why has the wicked man renounced God? He says to himself, “You will never call me to account.”
Psa.10.13.kjv: Wherefore doth the wicked contemn God? he hath said in his heart, Thou wilt not require it.

Psa.50.21.bsb: You have done these things, and I kept silent; you thought I was just like you. But now I rebuke you and accuse you to your face.
Psa.50.21.kjv: These things hast thou done, and I kept silence; thou thoughtest that I was altogether such an one as thyself: but I will reprove thee, and set them in order before thine eyes.

Psa.73.9.bsb: They set their mouths against the heavens, and their tongues strut across the earth.
Psa.73.9.kjv: They set their mouth against the heavens, and their tongue walketh through the earth.

Psa.73.11.bsb: The wicked say, “How can God know? Does the Most High have knowledge?”
Psa.73.11.kjv: And they say, How doth God know? and is there knowledge in the most High?

Psa.74.18.bsb: Remember how the enemy has mocked You, O LORD, how a foolish people has spurned Your name.
Psa.74.18.kjv: Remember this, that the enemy hath reproached, O Lord, and that the foolish people have blasphemed thy name.

Psa.78.19.bsb: They spoke against God, saying, “Can God really prepare a table in the wilderness?
Psa.78.19.kjv: Yea, they spake against God; they said, Can God furnish a table in the wilderness?

Psa.78.20.bsb: When He struck the rock, water gushed out and torrents raged. But can He also give bread or supply His people with meat?”
Psa.78.20.kjv: Behold, he smote the rock, that the waters gushed out, and the streams overflowed; can he give bread also? can he provide flesh for his people?

Psa.94.7.bsb: They say, “The LORD does not see; the God of Jacob pays no heed.”
Psa.94.7.kjv: Yet they say, The Lord shall not see, neither shall the God of Jacob regard it.

Psa.139.20.bsb: who speak of You deceitfully; Your enemies take Your name in vain.
Psa.139.20.kjv: For they speak against thee wickedly, and thine enemies take thy name in vain.

Psa.10.6.bsb: He says to himself, “I will not be moved; from age to age I am free of distress.”
Psa.10.6.kjv: He hath said in his heart, I shall not be moved: for I shall never be in adversity.

Psa.14.1.bsb: For the choirmaster. Of David. The fool says in his heart, “There is no God.” They are corrupt; their acts are vile. There is no one who does good.
Psa.14.1.kjv: To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David. The fool hath said in his heart, There is no God. They are corrupt, they have done abominable works, there is none that doeth good.

Psa.14.4.bsb: Will the workers of iniquity never learn? They devour my people like bread; they refuse to call upon the LORD.
Psa.14.4.kjv: Have all the workers of iniquity no knowledge? who eat up my people as they eat bread, and call not upon the Lord.

Psa.73.2.bsb: But as for me, my feet had almost stumbled; my steps had nearly slipped.
Psa.73.2.kjv: But as for me, my feet were almost gone; my steps had well nigh slipped.

Psa.73.3.bsb: For I envied the arrogant when I saw the prosperity of the wicked.
Psa.73.3.kjv: For I was envious at the foolish, when I saw the prosperity of the wicked.

Psa.73.4.bsb: They have no struggle in their death; their bodies are well-fed.
Psa.73.4.kjv: For there are no bands in their death: but their strength is firm.

Psa.73.5.bsb: They are free of the burdens others carry; they are not afflicted like other men.
Psa.73.5.kjv: They are not in trouble as other men; neither are they plagued like other men.

Psa.73.6.bsb: Therefore pride is their necklace; a garment of violence covers them.
Psa.73.6.kjv: Therefore pride compasseth them about as a chain; violence covereth them as a garment.

Psa.73.7.bsb: From their prosperity proceeds iniquity; the imaginations of their hearts run wild.
Psa.73.7.kjv: Their eyes stand out with fatness: they have more than heart could wish.

Psa.73.8.bsb: They mock and speak with malice; with arrogance they threaten oppression.
Psa.73.8.kjv: They are corrupt, and speak wickedly concerning oppression: they speak loftily.

Psa.73.10.bsb: So their people return to this place and drink up waters in abundance.
Psa.73.10.kjv: Therefore his people return hither: and waters of a full cup are wrung out to them.

Psa.73.12.bsb: Behold, these are the wicked—always carefree as they increase their wealth.
Psa.73.12.kjv: Behold, these are the ungodly, who prosper in the world; they increase in riches.

Psa.73.13.bsb: Surely in vain I have kept my heart pure; in innocence I have washed my hands.
Psa.73.13.kjv: Verily I have cleansed my heart in vain, and washed my hands in innocency.

Psa.73.14.bsb: For I am afflicted all day long and punished every morning.
Psa.73.14.kjv: For all the day long have I been plagued, and chastened every morning.

Psa.73.15.bsb: If I had said, “I will speak this way,” then I would have betrayed Your children.
Psa.73.15.kjv: If I say, I will speak thus; behold, I should offend against the generation of thy children.

Psa.73.16.bsb: When I tried to understand all this, it was troublesome in my sight
Psa.73.16.kjv: When I thought to know this, it was too painful for me;

Psa.73.17.bsb: until I entered God’s sanctuary; then I discerned their end.
Psa.73.17.kjv: Until I went into the sanctuary of God; then understood I their end.

Psa.73.18.bsb: Surely You set them on slick ground; You cast them down into ruin.
Psa.73.18.kjv: Surely thou didst set them in slippery places: thou castedst them down into destruction.

Psa.73.19.bsb: How suddenly they are laid waste, completely swept away by terrors!
Psa.73.19.kjv: How are they brought into desolation, as in a moment! they are utterly consumed with terrors.

Psa.73.20.bsb: Like one waking from a dream, so You, O Lord, awaken and despise their form.
Psa.73.20.kjv: As a dream when one awaketh; so, O Lord, when thou awakest, thou shalt despise their image.

Psa.73.21.bsb: When my heart was grieved and I was pierced within,
Psa.73.21.kjv: Thus my heart was grieved, and I was pricked in my reins.

Psa.73.22.bsb: I was senseless and ignorant; I was a brute beast before You.
Psa.73.22.kjv: So foolish was I, and ignorant: I was as a beast before thee.

Psa.73.23.bsb: Yet I am always with You; You hold my right hand.
Psa.73.23.kjv: Nevertheless I am continually with thee: thou hast holden me by my right hand.

Psa.73.25.bsb: Whom have I in heaven but You? And on earth I desire no one besides You.
Psa.73.25.kjv: Whom have I in heaven but thee? and there is none upon earth that I desire beside thee.

Psa.73.26.bsb: My flesh and my heart may fail, but God is the strength of my heart and my portion forever.
Psa.73.26.kjv: My flesh and my heart faileth: but God is the strength of my heart, and my portion for ever.

Psa.79.6.bsb: Pour out Your wrath on the nations that do not acknowledge You, on the kingdoms that refuse to call on Your name,
Psa.79.6.kjv: Pour out thy wrath upon the heathen that have not known thee, and upon the kingdoms that have not called upon thy name.

Psa.82.5.bsb: They do not know or understand; they wander in the darkness; all the foundations of the earth are shaken.
Psa.82.5.kjv: They know not, neither will they understand; they walk on in darkness: all the foundations of the earth are out of course.

Psa.92.6.bsb: A senseless man does not know, and a fool does not understand,
Psa.92.6.kjv: A brutish man knoweth not; neither doth a fool understand this.

Psa.94.8.bsb: Take notice, O senseless among the people! O fools, when will you be wise?
Psa.94.8.kjv: Understand, ye brutish among the people: and ye fools, when will ye be wise?

Psa.119.18.bsb: Open my eyes that I may see wondrous things from Your law.
Psa.119.18.kjv: Open thou mine eyes, that I may behold wondrous things out of thy law.

Psa.45.10.bsb: Listen, O daughter! Consider and incline your ear: Forget your people and your father’s house,
Psa.45.10.kjv: Hearken, O daughter, and consider, and incline thine ear; forget also thine own people, and thy father’s house;

Psa.45.12.bsb: The Daughter of Tyre will come with a gift; men of wealth will seek your favor.
Psa.45.12.kjv: And the daughter of Tyre shall be there with a gift; even the rich among the people shall intreat thy favour.

Psa.45.15.bsb: They are led in with joy and gladness; they enter the palace of the king.
Psa.45.15.kjv: With gladness and rejoicing shall they be brought: they shall enter into the king’s palace.

Psa.45.16.bsb: Your sons will succeed your fathers; you will make them princes throughout the land.
Psa.45.16.kjv: Instead of thy fathers shall be thy children, whom thou mayest make princes in all the earth.

Psa.45.17.bsb: I will commemorate your name through all generations; therefore the nations will praise you forever and ever.
Psa.45.17.kjv: I will make thy name to be remembered in all generations: therefore shall the people praise thee for ever and ever.

Psa.44.12.bsb: You sell Your people for nothing; no profit do You gain from their sale.
Psa.44.12.kjv: Thou sellest thy people for nought, and dost not increase thy wealth by their price.

Psa.106.46.bsb: He made them objects of compassion to all who held them captive.
Psa.106.46.kjv: He made them also to be pitied of all those that carried them captives.

Psa.128.2.bsb: For when you eat the fruit of your labor, blessings and prosperity will be yours.
Psa.128.2.kjv: For thou shalt eat the labour of thine hands: happy shalt thou be, and it shall be well with thee.

Psa.128.3.bsb: Your wife will be like a fruitful vine flourishing within your house, your sons like olive shoots sitting around your table.
Psa.128.3.kjv: Thy wife shall be as a fruitful vine by the sides of thine house: thy children like olive plants round about thy table.

Psa.128.4.bsb: In this way indeed shall blessing come to the man who fears the LORD.
Psa.128.4.kjv: Behold, that thus shall the man be blessed that feareth the Lord.

Psa.128.6.bsb: that you may see your children’s children. Peace be upon Israel!
Psa.128.6.kjv: Yea, thou shalt see thy children’s children, and peace upon Israel.

Psa.131.2.bsb: Surely I have stilled and quieted my soul; like a weaned child with his mother, like a weaned child is my soul within me.
Psa.131.2.kjv: Surely I have behaved and quieted myself, as a child that is weaned of his mother: my soul is even as a weaned child.

Psa.37.28.bsb: For the LORD loves justice and will not forsake His saints. They are preserved forever, but the offspring of the wicked will be cut off.
Psa.37.28.kjv: For the Lord loveth judgment, and forsaketh not his saints; they are preserved for ever: but the seed of the wicked shall be cut off.

Psa.107.38.bsb: He blesses them, and they multiply greatly; He does not let their herds diminish.
Psa.107.38.kjv: He blesseth them also, so that they are multiplied greatly; and suffereth not their cattle to decrease.

Psa.107.41.bsb: But He lifts the needy from affliction and increases their families like flocks.
Psa.107.41.kjv: Yet setteth he the poor on high from affliction, and maketh him families like a flock.

Psa.113.9.bsb: He settles the barren woman in her home as a joyful mother to her children. Hallelujah!
Psa.113.9.kjv: He maketh the barren woman to keep house, and to be a joyful mother of children. Praise ye the Lord.

Psa.127.3.bsb: Children are indeed a heritage from the LORD, and the fruit of the womb is His reward.
Psa.127.3.kjv: Lo, children are an heritage of the Lord: and the fruit of the womb is his reward.

Psa.10.14.bsb: But You have regarded trouble and grief; You see to repay it by Your hand. The victim entrusts himself to You; You are the helper of the fatherless.
Psa.10.14.kjv: Thou hast seen it; for thou beholdest mischief and spite, to requite it with thy hand: the poor committeth himself unto thee; thou art the helper of the fatherless.

Psa.10.18.bsb: to vindicate the fatherless and oppressed, that the men of the earth may strike terror no more.
Psa.10.18.kjv: To judge the fatherless and the oppressed, that the man of the earth may no more oppress.

Psa.27.10.bsb: Though my father and mother forsake me, the LORD will receive me.
Psa.27.10.kjv: When my father and my mother forsake me, then the Lord will take me up.

Psa.68.5.bsb: A father of the fatherless and a defender of widows is God in His holy habitation.
Psa.68.5.kjv: A father of the fatherless, and a judge of the widows, is God in his holy habitation.

Psa.146.9.bsb: The LORD protects foreigners; He sustains the fatherless and the widow, but the ways of the wicked He frustrates.
Psa.146.9.kjv: The Lord preserveth the strangers; he relieveth the fatherless and widow: but the way of the wicked he turneth upside down.

Psa.127.4.bsb: Like arrows in the hand of a warrior, so are children born in one’s youth.
Psa.127.4.kjv: As arrows are in the hand of a mighty man; so are children of the youth.

Psa.127.5.bsb: Blessed is the man whose quiver is full of them. He will not be put to shame when he confronts the enemies at the gate.
Psa.127.5.kjv: Happy is the man that hath his quiver full of them: they shall not be ashamed, but they shall speak with the enemies in the gate.

Psa.119.9.bsb: How can a young man keep his way pure? By guarding it according to Your word.
Psa.119.9.kjv: ב BETH. Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? by taking heed thereto according to thy word.

Psa.148.12.bsb: young men and maidens, old and young together.
Psa.148.12.kjv: Both young men, and maidens; old men, and children:

Psa.148.13.bsb: Let them praise the name of the LORD, for His name alone is exalted; His splendor is above the earth and the heavens.
Psa.148.13.kjv: Let them praise the name of the Lord: for his name alone is excellent; his glory is above the earth and heaven.

Psa.34.11.bsb: Come, children, listen to me; I will teach you the fear of the LORD.
Psa.34.11.kjv: Come, ye children, hearken unto me: I will teach you the fear of the Lord.

Psa.78.1.bsb: A Maskil of Asaph. Give ear, O my people, to my instruction; listen to the words of my mouth.
Psa.78.1.kjv: Maschil of Asaph. Give ear, O my people, to my law: incline your ears to the words of my mouth.

Psa.78.3.bsb: that we have heard and known and our fathers have relayed to us.
Psa.78.3.kjv: Which we have heard and known, and our fathers have told us.

Psa.78.4.bsb: We will not hide them from their children but will declare to the next generation the praises of the LORD and His might and the wonders He has performed.
Psa.78.4.kjv: We will not hide them from their children, shewing to the generation to come the praises of the Lord, and his strength, and his wonderful works that he hath done.

Psa.78.5.bsb: For He established a testimony in Jacob and appointed a law in Israel, which He commanded our fathers to teach to their children,
Psa.78.5.kjv: For he established a testimony in Jacob, and appointed a law in Israel, which he commanded our fathers, that they should make them known to their children:

Psa.78.6.bsb: that the coming generation would know them—even children yet to be born—to arise and tell their own children
